report.root_cause: lb-sandbox’s backend configuration change 62b6cafd switched the pool to unavailable ports 9991–9993 shortly before the renewed data-path errors; runtime loading of that config is not independently confirmed.

ruled_out.hypothesis: A bad deploy or code regression in lb-sandbox caused the failures.
A latent data-path code defect triggered by fault injection is the leading cause.
The 8093–8095 backend group was entirely down at the renewed error onset.
The earlier backend-pool changes explain the current onset.

ranked.root_cause: lb-sandbox configuration 62b6cafd selected unavailable backend ports 9991–9993, leaving the data path without its intended healthy pool.
The deliberate stop of nsbox-lb.service near onset may have contributed, but available lifecycle evidence does not establish its duration or restart sequence.

findings.question: What exact lb-sandbox data-path probe failures or related metric changes began at 04:21:05 UTC, and do they identify an affected port/backend?
findings.summary: Metrics show intermittent lb-sandbox probe/backend failures in the last 30 minutes, but sampled timestamps do not place a new failure exactly at 04:21:05 UTC (Unix 1790482865). At 04:21:05 the sampled backend_healthy 8094 series is low at 04:21:10 (0 versus prior 1 at 04:20:??), then recovers to 1 at 04:21:20; exact onset is bounded by sparse samples. Failures involve backend ports 8093/8094/8095 at other intervals, with 8094 showing repeated unhealthy states; admin probe timeouts are about 4 seconds intermittently. Current last values recover (backend_up all 1, upstream healthy 3, admin probe ~0.0004), while lb-sandbox p99 is elevated in anomaly summary by 1.5x, started 04:06:41 UTC (not 04:21:05). Evidence is insufficient to attribute a precise new probe failure or onset exactly to 04:21:05.
